environment.description: Same Flask application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB has AWS WAF v2 WebACL attached with the following rule groups evaluated in priority order: (1) AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet with SizeRestrictions_QUERYSTRING rule in COUNT mode only, (2) a custom rule group 'hr-app-query-sanitization' with a single rule using a RegexPatternSet that matches SqliRegexPatternSet (patterns: (?i)(union\s+select|;\s*drop|'\s*or\s*'|--\s*$|/\*|\*/|0x[0-9a-f]+|char\(|concat\()) applied to QueryString with BLOCK action and priority 1, (3) AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet with all rules in BLOCK mode at priority 2. Additionally, the ALB access logs are shipped to CloudWatch but this is monitoring only. The ECS task role has no relevance to the SQL injection vector. Note: the custom regex rule alone would miss some injection variants, and the AWS managed SQLi ruleset alone has known false-negative edge cases with SQLite-specific syntax, but together they provide overlapping coverage.

config.load_balancer: AWS ALB with WAF v2 WebACL
config.network: Private subnet, ALB in public subnet
